authors.bio: Rudolph J. Kryger has been involved in television broadcasting since 1958. He began his career with CKLW TV in Windsor, Ontario, and continued in the same premises through several ownership changes, resulting in the acquisition of the station by the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation in 1975. During this period, he progressed through the technical ranks from studio systems maintenance to VTR specialist. Several noteworthy accomplishments include the design of a mini-mobile unit, a time-code generator and a frame-accurate digital videotape editor for which he received an award from the Canadian Association of Broadcasters in 1972. In 1974, he was promoted to the position of Chief Engineer and is currently the Manager of Maintenance/Engineering Services. As an active member of the SMPTE since 1973, he served on the Detroit Section as Test Materials Advisor, Board Manager, Sec'y/Treasurer and Chairman for two terms. In 1983, he was instrumental in encompassing part of Southwestern Ontario, Canada, within the geographic area of the Detroit Section. He was recently elected as a member to the Board of Governors, and served as Program Chairman for the 25th Televison Conference.
